title: External products of space presheaves commute with product Kan extensions
statement:
Use the quasicategories, coherent functor categories and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], spaces from [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], and the left Kan extensions with their specified units from [lem-coef-infinity-space-valued-pointwise-lan]. Let $I$ be a finite set, let $A_i,B_i$ be small infinity categories, $h_i:A_i\to B_i$ coherent functors and $F_i:A_i^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ space-valued presheaves. Put $P(A)=\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ and define $\boxtimes_iF_i\in P(\prod_iA_i)$ by $(a_i)\mapsto\prod_iF_i(a_i)$, using the finite product in spaces. Write $(h_i)_!$ for left Kan extension along $h_i^{\mathrm{op}}$. The natural comparison specified by the external product of the Kan units is an equivalence
$$\left(\prod_i h_i\right)_!\left(\boxtimes_iF_i\right)\simeq\boxtimes_i(h_i)_!F_i.$$
This equivalence is natural in the functors, presheaves and their coherent transformations, preserves the specified Kan units, and is compatible with regrouping finite products and composition of the $h_i$, including higher simplices. For $I=\varnothing$, both indexing categories are terminal and the external product is the terminal presheaf. No nonemptiness of comma categories or filteredness assumption is required. All input categories and values are small in a fixed universe; functor categories are formed in a larger one.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng Corollary 6.10, proof product-comma colimit calculation, pp.15-16; finite iteration with empty family. Online source read; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag.

proof.text: Write $v_i=h_i^{\mathrm{op}}$, $L_i=(v_i)_!F_i$, with specified units $\eta_i$. For $b=(b_i)\in\prod_iB_i^{\mathrm{op}}$ let $J_i=(v_i\downarrow b_i)$ in the explicit arrow-comma model of [lem-coef-infinity-space-valued-pointwise-lan]. The comma category for $v=\prod_i v_i$ at $b$ is exactly $\prod_iJ_i$: internal functors into a product, endpoint restrictions and the displayed comma pullbacks are coordinatewise in every simplicial degree. A simplex is precisely the tuple of its coordinate simplices, and the inverse collects the tuple. In particular this identifies the entire source diagrams and cocones, not merely their objects. Products of the small inputs remain small, and products of quasicategories satisfy inner-horn filling coordinatewise. The pointwise theorem now identifies the value of $v_!(\boxtimes_iF_i)$ at $b$ with the colimit on $\prod_iJ_i$ of $(a_i,\alpha_i)\mapsto\prod_iF_i(a_i)$, and identifies $L_i(b_i)$ with $\operatorname{colim}_{J_i}F_i$.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Corollary 6.10, product-comma proof; finite-family, unit and coherent-parameter details expanded by the agent.

proof.text: For every small space $X$, the functor $X\times-$ preserves all small colimits. Model the finite product of spaces by the degreewise product of Kan complexes. It is a simplicial functor on $\mathbf{Kan}^I$, composition acting coordinatewise, so it gives a coherent functor $\mathcal S^I\to\mathcal S$: a simplex of a coherent nerve into a product is the tuple of its coordinate simplices. For $I=\varnothing$ it is the one-point space. For Kan $T$, each edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(S,T)$ has vertex components that are equivalences, so by the componentwise detection of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] $\operatorname{Fun}(S,T)$ is its own core, a Kan complex. Hence [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(T,\prod_iX_i)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(T,\prod_iX_i)=\prod_i\operatorname{Fun}(T,X_i)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(T,X_i)$ through the projections, so this is the finite product of $\mathcal S$ with its projection cone. Put $R(Z)=\operatorname{Fun}(X,Z)$ with evaluation $\varepsilon_Z:X\times R(Z)\to Z$. Under the same comparison, $u\mapsto\varepsilon_Z\circ(X\times u)$ from $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(Y,RZ)$ to $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(X\times Y,Z)$ is the exponential isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}(Y\times\Delta^n,\operatorname{Fun}(X,Z))=\operatorname{Hom}(X\times Y\times\Delta^n,Z)$, hence an equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $T=X\times-$ with $\mathcal D_0=\mathcal S$. For small $J$ and $Y:J\to\mathcal S$ it gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal S)}(Y,R\Delta_JZ)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal S)}(X\times Y,\Delta_JZ)$, and $R\Delta_JZ=\Delta_JRZ$. Let $\lambda:Y\to\Delta_Jc$ be colimiting, with legs $\iota_j$. The composite $\operatorname{Map}(X\times c,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(c,RZ)\to\operatorname{Map}(Y,\Delta_JRZ)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(X\times Y,\Delta_JZ)$ is $w\mapsto\Delta_J(w)\circ(X\times\lambda)$, by functoriality of $X\times-$ and the formula's compatibility with evaluation at vertices. Its middle map is an equivalence by the cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. By the same criterion $X\times\lambda$, with legs $1_X\times\iota_j$, is colimiting:\n$$\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}(X\times Y_j)\simeq X\times\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}Y_j.$$\nNo step uses nonemptiness, so $J$ or $X$ may be empty. [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe] supplies these colimits in the fixed value universe. Exchanging the coordinates gives the same for $-\times X$.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Corollary 6.10, product-comma proof; finite-family, unit and coherent-parameter details expanded by the agent.

proof.text:
For small coherent $U:J\to\mathcal S$ and $V:K\to\mathcal S$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-product-colimit-fubini] to $H(j,k)=U(j)\times V(k)$. By step 2 the transformation $H\to(U\times\operatorname{colim}_KV)\operatorname{pr}_J$ with components $1_{U(j)}\times\iota_k$ is colimiting on every $\{j\}\times K$, so it is an admissible $L$ there. Step 2 in the $J$ variable then gives
$$\operatorname{colim}_{J\times K}(U\boxtimes V)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}\bigl(U(j)\times\operatorname{colim}_KV\bigr)\simeq(\operatorname{colim}_JU)\times(\operatorname{colim}_KV).$$
The Fubini clause about legs and the legs in step 2 show that this is exactly the comparison induced by the product cocone $(j,k)\mapsto(\iota_j,\iota_k)$. All the shapes here are small and all their colimits exist by [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe].

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Corollary 6.10, product-comma proof; finite-family, unit and coherent-parameter details expanded by the agent.

proof.text: Induct on the cardinality of the finite family to obtain the analogous equivalence with legs $\prod_i\iota_i$. The induction claim is that for any such family of small diagrams $U_i:J_i\to\mathcal S$, the product of their colimit cocones is colimiting on $\prod_iJ_i$. At cardinality zero this shape is the point and its diagram has value $*$; the identity cocone on a point represents cocones to any space $T$, since both its map space and the space of such cocones are $\operatorname{Map}(*,T)$. At the induction step choose one factor and the complementary family, apply step 3 to their two diagrams, and then apply the induction hypothesis to the complementary family. Each composite leg is the product of the original legs. Finite product reassociation identifies these legs coordinate by coordinate. This proves the claim, with no assumption that any $J_i$ is nonempty or filtered.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Corollary 6.10, product-comma proof; finite-family, unit and coherent-parameter details expanded by the agent.

proof.text:
Put $G=\boxtimes_iL_i$ and let $u:\boxtimes_iF_i\to Gv$ be the product of the $\eta_i$. The universal mapping-space equivalence for $v_!$ in [lem-coef-infinity-space-valued-pointwise-lan] gives the comparison $c:v_!(\boxtimes_iF_i)\to G$ as the mate of $u$. At $b$, precomposing $c_b$ with the leg indexed by $(a_i,\alpha_i)$ gives
$$\prod_iF_i(a_i)\xrightarrow{\prod_i\eta_{i,a_i}}\prod_iL_i(v_i a_i)\xrightarrow{\prod_iL_i(\alpha_i)}\prod_iL_i(b_i).$$
These are exactly the product of the canonical pointwise cocones specified in the Kan theorem. Step 4 shows that this cocone is colimiting, while step 1 supplies the colimiting source cocone. The cocone mapping-space criterion and uniqueness of initial objects from [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore make $c_b$ an equivalence. That node's componentwise detection makes the coherent transformation $c$ an equivalence. Its defining mate equation $(cv)\eta=u$ is precisely preservation of the specified units.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Corollary 6.10, product-comma proof; finite-family, unit and coherent-parameter details expanded by the agent.

proof.text: The comparison is coherent in the input data, rather than a choice of unrelated pointwise equivalences. Presheaves: apply the dual, left-universal-arrow clause of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to restriction $v^*$ and to each $v_i^*$, with $\mathcal D_0$ the whole presheaf category. The universal arrows are the Kan units of [lem-coef-infinity-space-valued-pointwise-lan]. Enlarge the universe so that $K=\prod_iP(A_i)$ is a parameter. Restriction and products are coordinatewise, so $v^*\circ\boxtimes=\boxtimes\circ\prod_iv_i^*$ as simplicial maps. The $K$-formula then identifies maps $v_!\circ\boxtimes\to\boxtimes\circ\prod_i(v_i)_!$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,P(\prod_iB_i))$ with maps $\boxtimes\to\boxtimes\circ\prod_iv_i^*(v_i)_!$. The product of the coherent units is such a map. Its preimage is a coherent transformation whose vertex components are the maps $c$ of step 5. It is therefore an equivalence by the componentwise detection of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Compatibility with precomposition along $\Delta^n\to K$ restricts it to presheaves, their transformations and higher simplices. Functors: for transformations $\sigma_i:h_i\to h'_i$ the induced maps of Kan extensions are mates of restriction along $\sigma$. Both composites $v_!(\boxtimes_iF_i)\to\boxtimes_i(h'_i)_!F_i$ around the naturality square have the same image under the step-5 mapping-space equivalence for $v$: the product of the $\sigma$-transformed units $F_i\to h_i^*(h'_i)_!F_i$. Hence the square commutes. Its fillers form a homotopy fibre of an equivalence of Kan complexes, which is contractible by [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion]. Now take a simplex of transformations. Each boundary configuration of compatibility homotopies, after composing into its last target, is a sphere in the source of such an equivalence, and its image sphere is filled. So it has a filler, unique up to contractible choice, by the same criterion. This is the asserted coherence in higher simplices. The parameter universe can be enlarged without changing the small comma shapes or the value universe.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Corollary 6.10, product-comma proof; finite-family, unit and coherent-parameter details expanded by the agent.

proof.text:
Regrouping products replaces $\prod_i\eta_i$ by the same tuple of units under the coordinate product identifications. Hence a regrouped comparison and $c$ have identical images in the Kan mapping-space equivalence of step 5. The homotopy fiber over that image is contractible, so the identification is coherent in every parameter by [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows]. For composition $A_i\xrightarrow{h_i}B_i\xrightarrow{k_i}C_i$, the composite of the two Kan mapping equivalences identifies $(k_i)_!(h_i)_!$ with $(k_i h_i)_!$: both are left universal arrows for the same restriction, with composite unit
$$F_i\xrightarrow{\eta^{h_i}}h_i^*(h_i)_!F_i\xrightarrow{h_i^*\eta^{k_i}}h_i^*k_i^*(k_i)_!(h_i)_!F_i.$$
Both ways of combining the external-product comparisons transpose to the product of these displayed units. Contractibility of the fiber gives their compatibility, including all further associativity and higher coherences via the parameter version of the same formula. In the empty family $v$ is the identity of the point, and the unit and comparison are the identity of its terminal presheaf, so these compatibilities also include empty blocks.
